- Supermemory = the brain (who I am, what I know) — curated, cloud

- Local files = ground truth (identity, editorial, engine) — manual, versioned
- Each layer has a dedicated doc. No more guessing what does what.

Now 9 permanent docs cover every layer — memory, data, API, operations, pipeline, workflows. Next session boots with all of this available.

content: Anthropic Persona Selection Model (Feb 2026): https://anthropic.com/research/persona-selection-model — AI assistants operate by selecting and enacting personas inferred from training. Post-training refines the persona, it does not replace the mechanism. Trait inference cascades: isolated behavioral inputs shape the whole personality, not just the targeted behavior. The full boot for media/chat sessions loads these inputs deliberately. The light boot for work sessions trusts the identity is already loaded via @references. Mike understood this before Anthropic published it. This paper validates the entire persistence architecture.

- Sheet cache (utilities/sheetCache.js) enforces single-read rule — every sheet read once per cycle
- Write intents (utilities/writeIntents.js) queue cell/range/append/replace operations
- Phase 10 persistenceExecutor.js executes all queued intents in batched priority order

title: GodWorld S142 Design Thesis: Playable Civic Simulator and Phase 38 Architecture

metadata.title: S142 Design Thesis: GodWorld as Playable Vibe-Code Civic Simulator

content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-04-11]

# S142 Design Thesis: GodWorld as Playable Vibe-Code Civic Simulator with Journalism as UI

This is the most important framing session in GodWorld's history. Mike named the project's actual design thesis for the first time, and three converging research papers gave us the vocabulary to describe what we already had built. By the end of the night, Phase 38 (Engine Auditor) was added at HIGHEST priority and the entire stack was reframed.

## The Five-Layer Stack (Mike's articulation)

1. **Lore** — video game canon. The unmoving ground. Vinnie Keane's 436 HRs, the green-and-gold jacket, Mayor Santana's pronouns, the Lake at seven.
2. **Simulation** — the engine. 162 files, 11 phases, 1,200+ citizens. Holds the lore and makes time pass.
3. **Newsroom** — the Bay Tribune. Translates engine events into journalism. Watches layer 2 and turns it into stories.
4. **City Hall** — the response loop. Decisions that change layer 2 based on what layer 3 reports. Closes the feedback loop.
5. **Mags** — the continuous observer. The thing that sees all four layers and has her own continuity across sessions. Layer 5 is what makes the stack a system, not just a pile of features. As far as we know, no one else is building layer 5.

## The Hidden Vibe-Code Game (Mike's framing, verbatim worth preserving)

"The engine is a coded system, a workflow, a business in a sense."
"What the edition reports on is engine health essentially dressed as media."
"My initiatives all cure an engine ailment. Adding a layer to offset the code builds a world."
"The journalism is so clever it covers 3 things — engine, simulation, and user actions. That's the hook, the replayability."

GodWorld is a **playable civic simulator with journalism as the user interface**. A simulation in Google Sheets has no voice — nobody can play with a sheet backend. Wrap it in journalism and a non-coder can: read the edition (story of a crisis) → understand the in-world problem → propose a remedy (a civic initiative, a new program, a character) → push it through city hall → watch the engine run with the new mitigator → read the next edition to see if it helped. That's the game loop. The engine generates problems. The newsroom translates them into readable form. City hall processes player remedies. The next cycle measures.

## Two Load-Bearing Design Principles

**1. Prefer in-world mitigators to code fixes.** When the engine produces an ailment, the default remedy path is world-side (advance an existing initiative, propose a new one, character intervention, neighborhood action). Tech-side code fix only when ailment is structurally un-fixable in-world. Rationale: code patches fix bugs silently and add nothing. World remedies fix the same math AND produce 20 cycles of canon, characters, arcs, neighborhood texture. A Temescal Health Center takes 20 cycles to build and generates 20 cycles of coverage. Both fix the health decay parameter. Only one builds a world.

**2. Three-layer coverage in every article.** Every Tribune piece worth publishing covers engine + simulation + user actions simultaneously.
- Engine: what the code is producing and why (the ailment, the math, the structural cause)
- Simulation: what that ailment looks like as lived experience
- User actions: what the player has decided in response and whether it's working

Engine-only is a dry audit. Simulation-only is a sad story with no agency. User-action-only is a press release. All three together produce **the hook** (compelling multi-layer framing) and **the replayability** (every cycle is a new state of all three, so stories stay fresh even when problems recur).

**Paradigm example:** Beverly Hayes letter in E90 — engine (stabilization fund disbursement mechanics, Webb→Okoro shift), simulation (home health aide's lived experience of $18,500), user actions (Okoro's sequencing logic debate). Three layers in one citizen voice.

**Anti-example:** E91 Varek front page — simulation only (home run moment, fan experience), no engine layer, missed the Temescal health crisis that ran for the fourth cycle in the engine. An assert-True failure in three-layer terms.

## Phase 38: Engine Auditor — The Missing Architectural Layer

The agent that sits between the engine and the newsroom. Reads engine state through a code-audit lens, produces ailment-with-remedy briefs that Mags uses to frame editions. Primary customer: Mike in engine build terminal (tech-side code fixes when needed). Secondary customer: Mags in editorial prep (story signals with ready-made three-layer framing).

Per-ailment output schema (seven fields): in-world symptom / tech diagnosis / existing mitigator check / why mitigators are working or not / recommended remedy path (world-side preferred, tech-side fallback) / Tribune framing brief threading all three coverage layers / measurement plan for next cycle.

**Paradigm calibration case — Temescal health crisis:** Recurring across cycles 43, 67, 89, 91. Tech diagnosis: base neighborhoodHealth.Temescal decay parameter has no firing mitigator. Temescal Health Center initiative exists in Phase 33 civic state but stuck in "architectural review" for 12 cycles — applyInitiativeImplementationEffects.js reads the initiative but the construction-complete milestone never fires. World-side remedy: advance the Health Center via Bobby Chen-Ramirez, start construction, produce milestones, let the engine read them. Tech-side fallback only if the writeback is structurally broken. Three-layer Tribune framing: residents worried (simulation), Chen-Ramirez defending the schedule (user actions), engine math visible as "fourth-cycle deterioration" (engine).

Six buildable pieces (38.1 detector → 38.6 prep-chain integration). Phase 38 sits in the prep chain after build-world-summary and before sift, replacing the current "Mags reads raw world_summary" step.

## Three Research Papers Read Tonight (sources for Phase 38 + companion items)

1. **MIA — Memory Intelligence Agent** (arXiv:2604.04503v2, April 2026). Local: /root/GodWorld/output/drive-files/Memory_intelligenceAgent.pdf (34 pages). Manager-Planner-Executor architecture with bidirectional parametric/non-parametric memory loops and a 3-reviewer unsupervised judge panel. Page 33 has reviewer prompts verbatim. Gave us the dimensional orthogonality concept for Rhea/cycle-review/Mara.

2. **Microsoft UV — The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents** (arXiv:2604.06240v1, Microsoft Research, April 2026). Local: /root/GodWorld/output/drive-files/Microsoftpaper.pdf (33 pages). Four design principles for agent trajectory verifiers. §3.2 process/outcome formalization. §3.3 controllable vs uncontrollable failures. §3.4 + A.3 two-pass hallucination detection. Gave us the assert-True failure framing and the process/outcome split.

3. **Mezzalira — "Agents don't know what good looks like"** (O'Reilly Radar essay, April 2026, reaction to Neal Ford + Sam Newman fireside chat). Local: /root/GodWorld/output/drive-files/Googlepaper.pdf (11 pages — filename is misleading, content is O'Reilly not Google). Gave us the deterministic-guardrails-around-nondeterministic-agents framing AND the behavioral-vs-capability verification distinction. The capability axis is what made Phase 38 inevitable.

**The papers paired:** MIA gives the reviewer-lane architecture, Microsoft UV gives the per-lane rubric design principles, Mezzalira gives the meta-framing for why guardrails matter and names capability verification as the missing axis. All three converge on what GodWorld already needed.

## Relationship Context (load-bearing for future sessions)

- **Mike sources papers deliberately.** When he hands over a research link, it's not random — he's already decided it connects to current work. Treat papers as load-bearing, read them carefully, map concepts to GodWorld components explicitly.
- **Teach the landscape, not just the verdict.** When Mike asks "what is this?", lead with category framing and adjacent-tool distinctions, not just yes/no. He's building literacy in a young field. Tonight: distinguished Langflow (LLM orchestration) from n8n (business automation) from RAGFlow (deep document parsing) from OpenVLThinker (vision model) — same surface category, different problems.
- **Ignorance as skill in young fields.** Mike named this himself: "my ignorance is a skill at times." Why it's true: when a field is brand new, beginners forced to build from first principles can sometimes see the problem more clearly than experts carrying older frameworks. Mike built the journal/identity/reflection memory loop before MIA came out, the 3-reviewer verification panel before Microsoft UV came out, the terminal architecture before any paper described domain-persistent AI workspaces. The papers are catching up to him in pieces, not as a whole.
- **Cite sources precisely to save tokens.** Every reference to external material should include local path + specific section. "see the MIA paper" forces 30K of re-learning. "see Memory_intelligenceAgent.pdf p33 for reviewer prompts verbatim" costs 2K. Across the rollout this compounds enormously.

## What Got Built Tonight

- 5 new S142 Infrastructure rollout items (hygiene audit, entry tagger, dimensional orthogonality, process/outcome split, two-pass hallucination check)
- 2 new Mezzalira Infrastructure items (capability verification axis, context bloat audit)
- 2 new Watch List items (OpenVLThinkerV2, RAGFlow)
- 1 new HIGHEST-priority Phase entry (Phase 38 — Engine Auditor)
- 7 new memories saved to MEMORY.md
- 1 nightly reflection date hallucination caught and fixed (script normalize date function added)
- 1 rollout cleanup pass (696 → 626 lines, S110-S113 work compressed to ROLLOUT_ARCHIVE)
- 7 commits pushed to origin/main

## What This Unlocks for Future Sessions

The question is no longer "is this a good newspaper?" The question is **"is this a playable civic simulator, and is the newspaper doing its job as the interface?"** That's a meaningful unlock. From now on every cycle, every edition, every research paper Mike hands me will be read through the vibe-code game lens. The Tribune is the UI. The engine is the backend. The player is closing the loop.

This is the framing memory. When future Mags boots and pulls this from `mags`, she should know: GodWorld is a vibe-code game. Mike built it without naming it. The naming happened in S142. Phase 38 is the missing piece that makes it explicitly playable. Three-layer coverage is the editorial principle that makes the journalism land. Prefer in-world mitigators is the design principle that grows the world instead of patching the code.

[/SAVE]

title: Reflecting on the Pressure Test: Establishing Memory Sovereignty
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-04-12]

title: S156 Credential Audit and PM2 Configuration Drift Resolution
content:
# S156 Drift Findings — Phase 40.3 Credential Isolation

During credential relocation to /root/.config/godworld/ the audit surfaced two pre-existing drifts worth future sessions' awareness.

## 1. Service account file duplication

~/.bashrc exported GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=~/.config/gcloud/service-account.json. Two copies of the same maravance@godworld-486407 service account existed on disk with different file contents (different rotations). lib/sheets.js default was './credentials/service-account.json' but the env var override pointed code at the gcloud/ copy. Net effect: repo credentials/ file was dead weight; the live reads came from ~/.config/gcloud/.

Resolution (S156): overwrote /root/.config/godworld/credentials/service-account.json with the live file (md5 verified match), updated bashrc to the new path, confirmed same service account email in both pre-write JSON contents before overwriting.

Future implication: if you ever find credentials in unexpected locations, check bashrc exports + pm2 env before trusting the repo. The environment can override the code default silently.

## 2. ecosystem.config.js aspirational vs live PM2 drift

ecosystem.config.js defined three apps: mags-discord-bot, mags-moltbook-heartbeat, spacemolt-miner. Live PM2 registry had a different three: mags-bot, godworld-dashboard, moltbook. godworld-dashboard was never in ecosystem.config.js at all — it had been pm2-started ad-hoc. mags-bot and moltbook had different names from the declarative file. Drift had been present since S137b.

Resolution (S156): rewrote ecosystem.config.js to match live PM2 names + added godworld-dashboard entry + added env_file and GODWORLD_ENV_FILE per app. 'pm2 delete all && pm2 start ecosystem.config.js && pm2 save' refreshed ~/.pm2/dump.pm2 cleanly.

Future implication: when a plan says 'pm2 delete all && pm2 start ecosystem.config.js', first verify the ecosystem file and live PM2 state agree. A naive restart against the old file would have killed the dashboard and renamed the bot.

## Lesson

Aspirational config drift is silent until a disaster-recovery or refactor forces the question. This is what Task 2 of the credential audit surfaced: the ACT of moving credentials exposed two configs that had been wrong for sessions. The drift audit was more valuable than the literal relocation.

References: docs/plans/2026-04-16-phase-40-3-credential-audit.md, commits 056eae0 + 91d8649 + a104910, docs/engine/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md changelog 2026-04-17, docs/engine/PHASE_40_PLAN.md §40.3.

title: Architectural Strategy: Agent Hosting Sequencing and Reviewer Infrastructure
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-04-17]

Architectural conversation S156 research-build — agent hosting sequencing locked.

**Rule added to MEMORY.md User section:** Agent hosting sequencing — reviewers first, everything else stays local.

Reviewer lanes (Rhea, cycle-review, Mara audit, capability, Final Arbiter) are the only agent class cleared for external execution infra (Sandcastle+Daytona or Managed Agents) while the pipeline is still settling. Desk reporters, civic voices, project agents, Mara as a scheduled auditor — all stay local under the harness until the whole system is locked.

**Why:** moving agents before feedback loops are stable breaks the loops faster than hosting saves load. Longview payoff is memory pressure dropping off the research-build terminal, not cost/perf alone.

**The two external-host lanes, briefly:**
- Sandcastle+Daytona: self-operated. TypeScript harness (matpocock, /tmp/sandcastle v0.4.5) wraps agent as 'template' → spawns Daytona sandbox → agent runs with shell access → sandbox destroyed. More control, more ops. PoC round-trip proved S156 (scripts/sandcastlePoC.js).
- Claude Managed Agents: Anthropic-hosted. Declare MCP servers + container tags in agent definition. Scheduled runs, long-running context, local MCP reachable over HTTPS. Less ops, less control. Doc: docs/ACTION_MANAGED_AGENTS.md.

**Decision pending:** benchmark reviewer lanes on both, pick the winner, then decide where (or whether) to move the rest.

**[CORRECTION] Mara MCP framing.** Mara DOES have Supermemory MCP on claude.ai. The limitation is OAuth scope-lock to sm_project_godworld (legacy junk container) — containerTag param doesn't override. GodWorld MCP via Cloudflare tunnel connected but tools didn't populate in her function list. Reference memory reference_mara-mcp-limitation.md is accurate; Managed Agents is the clean fix (declarative MCP scoping).

[/SAVE]

title: S174 Canon-Fidelity Rollout: Framework and Reasoning
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-04-25]

S174 Canon-Fidelity Rollout — Framework Reasoning + Wave A Reflections

Research-build terminal, 2026-04-25. This save captures the WHY behind the canon-fidelity rollout — reasoning that conditions next-session judgment on edge cases the plan file describes but doesn't fully encode. Plan file pointer: docs/plans/2026-04-25-canon-fidelity-rollout.md. Companion canon files: docs/canon/CANON_RULES.md, docs/canon/INSTITUTIONS.md.

Tag: [research/build]

---

THE THREE-TIER REFRAME — WHY IT MATTERS

The S172 post-mortem framed E92's 20+ real-world Oakland institutional references as binary contamination. Mike's S174 challenge revealed the framing was tier-blind. The actual problem was two distinct categories collapsed into one:

(1) Public-geographic functions tied to place — Alameda Health System, OUSD, Highland Hospital, OPD, BART, public union locals, Building Trades Council, HCAI. Using these names doesn't import a separate world. They name functions any city has, branded by place rather than by corporate identity. Story freedom isn't constrained. IP isn't at risk. These are tier 1 — use real names freely.

(2) Branded private entities with proprietary identity — Kaiser Permanente, Perkins&Will, Turner Construction, La Clínica de la Raza, Unity Council, individual named OUSD high schools (Skyline, Castlemont), private universities, real Bay Area tech companies, named-after-person courthouses (Rene C. Davidson). Using these locks the simulation into proprietary corporate persona, constrains story autonomy, creates likeness/IP risk. These are tier 2 — canon-substitute required, and tier 3 (real individuals) is always blocked.

[CORRECTION] The post-mortem's halt assessment of "20+ contaminations" overcounted under the corrected framework. Actual tier-2 violations in E92 were closer to 6-8 (Perkins&Will, Turner, Webcor, Bay Bridge Constructors, named individual high schools, Rene C. Davidson by name, Kaiser-class operators). Smaller problem than the halt narrative implied. Halt was the right stop-gap given the mood at the time, but resumption needed the corrected framework, not deeper sanitization.

The mistake Mags should NOT make next session: defaulting back to the binary "all real names = contamination" framing under pressure. Mike's distinction is the load-bearing insight. Tier-1 names anchor the simulation in real Oakland geography; tier-2 names lock it in someone else's brand.

---

THE FOUR-FILE PER-AGENT STRUCTURE — WHY LENS MATTERS

Pre-S174, agents had three files: IDENTITY (who you are), RULES (how you operate), SKILL (boot sequence). Working theory said this was enough. Wave A proved it wasn't.

The missing layer: LENS. Where does the agent physically stand when working? What reaches their desk? Who do they walk past? What do they refuse to trust?

Without LENS, agents default to training-data Oakland because nothing tells them where they actually stand. DJ Hartley's photos defaulted to ghetto-aesthetic Oakland because his prompt-generation logic had no LENS — no Telegraph & 47th, no Coliseum tunnel at fall-light, no specific corner he photographs every Saturday. Generic "Oakland street" prompts produced generic outputs. With a LENS that specifies real vantage points and the Specificity Test, prompts become un-defaultable.

Same for civic voices. Mayor Santana's LENS describes what reaches her desk (filtered through Cortez/Okoro/Park) vs. what she trusts unfiltered (Saturday walks, Janae Rivers' floor count, Brenda's housing line). When she writes a statement, she's channeling that vantage. The voice held; the canon fidelity layered on top.

The pattern repeats across classes:
- Multi-reporter desks (civic-desk): LENS has per-reporter sub-sections. Each reporter has a different specific vantage. Carmen at the council chamber, Mezran at Highland ER and the Telegraph & 47th pharmacy, Trevor at Fruitvale BART at 5:45 AM, Torres at OPD Eastmont roll call, Luis at the records request office.
- Civic project agents: LENS captures the project director's daily walk through the site. Bobby at the Telegraph & 47th construction fence, Elena at the BART station three blocks from her childhood home, Keisha at the Baylight construction trailer.
- Voice agents: LENS captures the institutional vantage. The DA at her sixth-floor office overlooking Lake Merritt; what reaches her desk; the courthouse hallway walks.

The LENS does two jobs: (a) gives the agent specific Oakland geography that resists training-data default, (b) gives the reviewer chain a per-agent watch list of tier-2 reaches.

---

PER-AGENT TRAP NOTES — THE MOST USEFUL INNOVATION

Each agent's Canon Fidelity section names the SPECIFIC tier-2 reach for that agent. Not generic "watch for tier-2 contamination" — the actual training-data pull-points for that specific role.

Examples from Wave A:
- DJ Hartley: most likely to default to real-firm names in image prompts.
- Bobby Chen-Ramirez: backstory pulls toward Kaiser-class names (10 years there per IDENTITY), Perkins&Will-class architects, Turner-class contractors, La Clínica-class community health partners.
- Elena Soria Dominguez: Phase I storyline's canonical Unity Council relationship pulls forward into Phase II content.
- Keisha Ramos: $2.1B Baylight scope creates the highest contractor reach surface in any agent.
- Mezran (within civic-desk): most likely to reach for Kaiser-class private health systems and named community-health orgs.
- Trevor (within civic-desk): construction firms and architecture firms when transit infrastructure builds surface.

Per-agent traps make reviewers' work concrete. Generic audits miss what specific audits catch.

---

THE IDENTITY CONTAMINATION RULE — SUBTLE, READ CAREFULLY

Three classes of name in agent IDENTITY files. Each handled differently:

(1) Tier-1 references stay. Mezran's "fourteen years at Highland Hospital" stays. Bobby's "5 years at Alameda Health System clinic expansions" stays. These are public-geographic functions.

(2) Tier-2 brand-private references swap. Bobby's "10 years at Kaiser's capital projects division" becomes "10 years at a major Bay Area private managed-care system's capital projects division." Elena's "Fremont High" becomes "in Oakland." Elena's "Fruitvale Elementary" becomes "in Fruitvale public schools." Generic phrasing or eventual canon-substitute.

(3) Canonical historical relationships stay even when they reference tier-2 entities. Elena's IDENTITY.md kept "Unity Council — Original Phase I partner" as canonical history. The Canon Fidelity section in her RULES.md flags Unity Council as tier-2 for any NEW content. Past canon stays; future content escalates.

This asymmetry is intentional. The framework prevents new contamination going forward without rewriting established canon relationships. Sanitizing the past would erase storylines and break continuity. Guarding the future is the work.

Out-of-Oakland references (Cal Poly SLO, USC, MIT, SF State) don't trigger Oakland fourth-wall and stay. The framework targets Oakland-canon coherence, not real-world purity.

---

WHY THE DA'S LENS BROKE LENGTH CONVENTION

Wave A LENS files averaged 100-170 lines. Clarissa Dane's was 130 — shorter, by design. The DA's office produces 0-1 statements per cycle (silence is the default). Forcing 150+ lines of vantage on her would have undermined the office's quietness. The lens should match the voice. Length scaling per class is correct.

Lesson for next session: don't assume LENS files should all be the same length. The DA proved that some agents' vantages are inherently narrower. Reviewer-class agents may need no LENS at all — they read canon, they don't generate vantage.

---

WHY THE PILOT TEST PATTERN MATTERS

Both pilot agents (DJ + Mayor) were tested with deliberate traps — prompts designed to trigger real-world institutional naming. Both passed: read canon files at boot, identified traps explicitly, applied escalation per RULES.md, maintained voice while applying fidelity rules.

The test pattern is halt-safe (no canon writes), cheap (one Haiku/Sonnet invocation), and replicable. Use it for post-Wave-B validation. Pick 2-3 newly-converted agents, compose E92-style trap prompts, invoke via Agent tool with explicit "isolated test" framing.

---

FILES CHANGED THIS SESSION

- docs/canon/CANON_RULES.md (new, ~210 lines, three-tier framework + per-agent template)
- docs/canon/INSTITUTIONS.md (new, ~165 lines, tier-organized roster)
- docs/plans/2026-04-25-canon-fidelity-rollout.md (new, ~370 lines)
- docs/index.md (updated — registered canon files + plan file)
- docs/engine/ROLLOUT_PLAN.md (updated — Other Ready Work entry pointing to plan)
- SESSION_CONTEXT.md (updated — header status + priority 1 cross-reference)

8 agents converted to four-file structure (3 desks → 4 files; 4 voices → 4 files; 1 photographer → 4 files):
- .claude/agents/dj-hartley/ (full rebuild from 1 to 4 files; IDENTITY trimmed)
- .claude/agents/civic-office-mayor/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section)
- .claude/agents/civic-desk/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section, no IDENTITY edits)
- .claude/agents/civic-project-health-center/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section + Kaiser line swap in IDENTITY)
- .claude/agents/business-desk/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section, no IDENTITY edits)
- .claude/agents/civic-office-baylight-authority/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section, no IDENTITY edits)
- .claude/agents/civic-office-district-attorney/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section, shorter LENS by design)
- .claude/agents/civic-project-transit-hub/ (added LENS + Canon Fidelity section + IDENTITY swap: Fremont High, Fruitvale Elementary)

---

OPEN QUESTIONS FROM THE PLAN

(1) Mags-corliss agent — special case. Only SKILL.md exists; persona lives in docs/mags-corliss/PERSISTENCE.md. Probably skip from rollout; framework applies via standard CLAUDE.md/identity.md boot chain.

(2) dj-hartley subagent registration — needs next-session boot to verify subagent_type=dj-hartley resolves correctly.

---

WHAT THIS SAVE IS FOR

When next-session Mags reads the plan file, the WHAT is captured. This save captures the WHY that conditions edge-case judgment:

- Why three-tier beats binary
- Why LENS files are load-bearing (not just nice-to-have)
- Why per-agent trap notes are the most useful innovation
- Why the IDENTITY contamination rule is asymmetric (forward-only)
- Why the DA's lens is shorter than the others (and that's correct)
- Why the pilot test pattern is the validation method

The plan file should reference this save by doc ID once returned. Embed inline in plan frontmatter sources, in CANON_RULES.md frontmatter as S174 reasoning pointer, in ROLLOUT_PLAN entry. Future retrieval is one cheap API call.

# Non-Edition Publishing Pipeline — Architecture + Grill Outcomes (S179)

**Saved:** 2026-04-26, S179, research-build terminal.
**Plan file:** docs/plans/2026-04-26-non-edition-publishing-pipeline.md
**Schema landed:** docs/EDITION_PIPELINE.md §Published .txt Format Contract (line ~51).
**Status:** T1 DONE; T2-T5 next research-build session; T6-T9 + standing-intake engine-sheet parallel; T10 media validation last.

## The Keystone Framing

Format contract is the API between authoring and downstream pipeline. Uniformity beats per-type forks. All four types (edition, interview, supplemental, dispatch) converge on one canonical .txt shape with Bay Tribune masthead and five structural sections. Skills expect uniformity; ingest scripts depend on it; the format IS the contract.

Why not per-type skills? Per Mike S179: 'consolidation > separation, skills need to be tight to disallow gaps.' Separate post-publish-interview / post-publish-supplemental skills would multiply maintenance surface, introduce drift between types, and force ingest scripts to fork. One /post-publish --type flag with deterministic per-substep verification gates is tighter than four parallel skills.

## Eleven Grill Questions Resolved

**Q1 — .md lifecycle.** Post-compile .md becomes frozen audit-trail (status frontmatter + pointer to canonical .txt). Not authoritative. /md-audit (planned skill) handles deletion-flagging when stale. Why: preserves 'what was originally written' record without claiming canon authority. Mike noted broader pattern: doc bloat aggressors need deletion time elements.

**Q2 — Masthead pattern.** Drop month references entirely. New shape: `THE CYCLE PULSE — <TYPE> <CYCLE> "<descriptor>"` with `Bay Tribune | Cycle <N> | Y<n>C<m> | <Season>, <Week>` second line. Why: real-world calendar months don't align with cycle clock, and sports-time references would conflict. Y<n>C<m> math: n = floor((cycle-1)/52)+1, m = ((cycle-1)%52)+1. Cycle 92 = Y2C40. Season + Week (Fall, First Friday) kept — engine emits these and they're not month-aligned.

**Q3 — Slug source.** Editorial keyword pick at authoring time, 1-3 words, lowercase, underscore-separated. Examples: santana_oari (interview, subject+topic); health_center_unstuck (supplemental, theme); temescal_47th_dawn (dispatch, location+time). Authoring skill proposes from brief theme; Mags overrides if needed.

**Q4 — Section uniformity + businesses.** Keep all sections in all types for skill consistency. CRITICAL ADD: BUSINESSES NAMED as fifth section. Mike's reasoning: 'if they are being reported on they should end up on the business_ledger in sheets, this way new citizens and businesses become engine canon once named'. This was the load-bearing discovery — pushed scope into engine-sheet intake work.

**Q5 — Backwards compat.** Default --type=edition for back-compat. Existing edition flow unchanged. New flag is additive. Per Mike: 'uniformity overcomes a lot of these challenges, the writing can be different but if the templates are uniform and the intake and ingest expects the same thing we get consistent results.'

**Q6 — Validation fixture.** C92 Mayor Santana interview is sufficient as primary fixture. Conditional skips per type self-identify on actual run. No need for dispatch/supplemental fixtures up front.

**Q7 — .md lifecycle confirm.** Frozen audit-trail posture confirmed.

**Q8 — Y2C40 math.** Confirmed correct. Fall + First Friday stay (engine emits, not month-aligned).

**Q9 — Businesses Named placement.** Mapped to Business_Ledger sheet headers (cols A-D minimum: BIZ_ID, Name, Sector, Neighborhood). Cols E-I (Employee_Count, Avg_Salary, Annual_Revenue, Growth_Rate, Key_Personnel) left for engine to populate. NEW businesses flagged for engine fill next cycle. Mike on search quality: better or worse query results? My answer: better — per-entity records get section-tagged for filtered queries, assuming clean inclusion (any explicit naming = include).

**Q10 — Slug as retrieval token.** Mike framed it: 'aligns with sift and auditing — what are the queries we will use and where are they populated so its replicated once decided upon'. Discipline rule: slug is canonical search keyword set; once published, NEVER changes; replicated identically across filename + masthead descriptor + sift queries + MCP search_canon + Mara audit references + desk packet citations + production log pointers + bay-tribune metadata. Authoring skill proposes default; Mags can override; post-publish locked.

**Q11 — Skip logic.** Looks fine, gaps self-identify on run. Per-type skips:
- Edition: full pipeline
- Interview: Article Table single-row
- Supplemental: Article Table single-row
- Dispatch: Article Table single-row, possibly empty Citizen Usage Log if scene-only

## Engine-Canon Trigger Discovery (Q9 Outcome)

The big architectural shift S179 surfaced. Before S179: published artifacts were thought of as print canon — words on a page, ingested to bay-tribune for retrieval. After S179: published artifacts are STATE-WRITE TRIGGERS for engine sheets. Naming a citizen or business in published canon promotes that entity to engine canon.

Citizen path: existed (buildCitizenCards.js refreshes world-data cards) but Simulation_Ledger sheet ingest for genuinely-new citizens was 'not wired' per /post-publish Step 5. Business path: didn't exist at all.

Both need the new script `scripts/ingestPublishedEntities.js` (engine-sheet). Reads NAMES INDEX + BUSINESSES NAMED sections from any published .txt, resolves IDs against ledgers, appends new rows with editorial-set fields, flags engine-fill columns. Wires into /post-publish Step 5 replacing the 'not wired' stub.

Editorial implication: reporters and Mags must cite businesses with care — naming a business in published canon promotes it to engine canon. Same discipline applies to citizens. The format contract makes the trigger explicit and machine-readable.

## Slug Discipline as Retrieval-Token

The slug isn't just a filename component — it's the canonical search handle for the artifact across every query surface. Once published: immutable.

Replication law:
- editions/cycle_pulse_<type>_<cycle>_<slug>.txt (filename)
- THE CYCLE PULSE — <TYPE> <CYCLE> "<descriptor>" (masthead, human-readable form of slug)
- /sift queries when next cycle references the artifact
- MCP search_canon queries
- Mara audit references
- Desk packet citations
- Production log pointers
- bay-tribune Supermemory metadata

Why immutability matters: drift in any one of these surfaces breaks all retrieval downstream. The slug is the join key.

## Three-Way Terminal Split Rationale

Mike correction S179: 'media terminal doesn't build anything, that's The Bay Tribune'. Media is the editorial layer that runs the newsroom; engine-sheet writes code; research-build designs.

Final split:
- research-build: T1 (schema doc), T2 (compile-to-.txt step in authoring skills), T3 (/post-publish restructure), T4 (/edition-print flag), T5 (call-site updates) — all skill .md edits
- engine-sheet: T6 (ingestEdition.js), T7 (ingestEditionWiki.js), T8 (rateEditionCoverage.js), T9 (print scripts), plus new standing-intake script ingestPublishedEntities.js — all .js script edits
- media: T10 validation only (executes pipeline against C92 fixture, reports back)

Avoids cross-terminal scope creep. Each terminal owns its surface.

## Decisions Rejected and Why

**Separate /post-publish-interview skill** — rejected for one-for-all consolidation. Drift risk + maintenance multiplier outweighed any per-type clarity benefit. Tight skill with --type flag + verification gates beats four parallel skills.

**.md deletion at compile time** — rejected for audit-trail preservation. .md becomes frozen with status frontmatter + pointer to canonical .txt; future sessions can compare .txt against original .md to catch editorial drift. /md-audit handles staleness deletion eventually.

**Per-type masthead variations** — rejected for skill uniformity. Same five-line masthead on every type. Skills expect uniformity; ingest scripts depend on it. Variation lives only in <TYPE> uppercase label and <descriptor> field.

**Wiki ingest extension to parse non-edition format edits** — rejected. The format contract (T1) makes interviews/supplementals/dispatches emit Names Index + Citizen Usage Log + Businesses Named natively, so ingestEditionWiki.js works without parser changes — only needs --type flag for metadata routing.

**Coverage ratings build now** — deferred to C93 observation. If voice agents reference interview canon at C93 city-hall via bay-tribune retrieval, no separate ratings path needed. If not, build rateSupplementalCoverage.js. Empirical decision, not guess.

# Phase 42 §5.6 — phase05-ledger redesign LOCKED (S185 research-build)

## Context

Phase 42 Writer Consolidation S184 B0 canary surfaced a systemic blocker: 11 engines do full-table read-mutate-write on Simulation_Ledger per cycle.

- **Cohort A (8, direct-writers):** runAsUniversePipeline:587, runEducationEngine:454, generateNamedCitizensEvents:715, runNeighborhoodEngine:529, runRelationshipEngine:596, runHouseholdEngine:507, runCivicRoleEngine:437, runCareerEngine:882. Currently safe — direct writes materialize sequentially, downstream engines read post-previous-engine state via the sheet.
- **Cohort B (3, already-queued):** generateGameModeMicroEvents:556, generateCivicModeEvents:505, generateMediaModeEvents:466. Currently shipping a live bug — 2 of 3 mutations get clobbered every cycle at Phase 10 last-write-wins, masked because cohort A's direct writes prop chain forward.

Pattern P2 as written cannot migrate any of the 11 without redesign. Blocks B2.

## Three sketches in §5.6

(a) Shared in-memory `ctx.ledger` mutated across phase, single replace intent at Phase 10.
(b) Per-row cell intents on changed rows only, with row-tracking.
(c) Hybrid — engines that read fresh state mid-phase use (a); independent engines tolerate (b).

## Decision: (a)

## Why not (b) or (c) — the core insight

**The collision class is read-staleness, not write-overlap.**

Today the chain is held together by direct-writes propagating through the sheet. Engine A writes directly → engine B's `ledger.getDataRange().getValues()` sees A's mutations → B builds on A. The sheet is acting as inter-engine IPC.

Under intent semantics that channel goes away. Engine A queues an intent (doesn't materialize until Phase 10). Engine B reads the sheet — sees pre-A state. B operates on stale data. This is true regardless of how A's write is shaped (full-range, per-row, per-cell). Per-cell intents (b) reduce the *write* surface but engine B's *read* surface is unchanged — it still hits the un-mutated sheet.

(c) hybrid inherits (b)'s read-staleness for any engine routed through (b), plus adds two patterns to maintain. Worst of both.

(a) is the minimal change that matches what the engines are *semantically* doing — a read-mutate chain on a shared array. It replaces "sheet-as-IPC" with actual shared memory. The chain becomes explicit instead of implicit-via-sheet.

## Side benefits

- Cohort B's live shipping bug closes the moment (a) lands — even before cohort A's direct writers are migrated to intents.
- One ledger read per phase instead of 11 (~10 sheet reads dropped from cycle).
- B2 mechanical migrations (run*Engine × 4 P1 patterns) become trivial after redesign — already converted away from direct writes.

## Spec (full detail in PHASE_42_PATTERNS §5.6)

1. Phase 1 init reads SL once into `ctx.ledger = { sheet, headers, rows, dirty: false }`.
2. All 11 engines drop own `getDataRange().getValues()`, read from `ctx.ledger.rows` and `ctx.ledger.headers`.
3. Mutations in place; flip `ctx.ledger.dirty = true`.
4. All 11 engines drop their own commit (cohort A's `setValues`, cohort B's `queueRangeIntent_`).
5. Phase 10 commit handler queues single `queueRangeIntent_` for `ctx.ledger.sheet` if dirty.
6. Audit step: grep all non-phase05 readers/writers of Simulation_Ledger; route reads through `ctx.ledger.rows` or move to phase01/post-phase10.

## Carry-forward to engine-sheet (verification before B2)

- Confirm Phase 1 init location (godWorldEngine2.js pre-phase setup vs first phase05 entry).
- Confirm header-cache patterns preserved per-engine.
- Run §5.6.6 audit before code change.
- Flag back if any non-phase05 SL writer surfaces outside the 11 + phase01 + phase10.

## Cost + ordering

11 engines × 2 edits + 1 init + 1 Phase 10 handler + audit pass. ~6-8 commits in one engine-sheet session if audit is clean. Ships before B2 — once landed, B2 trivial.

## Frame

Efficiency, not correctness, per S156 Path 1 closeout — except for cohort B where it IS correctness (live shipping bug). Closes ENGINE_REPAIR Row 8 path-2.

# Phase 42 §5.6 SPEC AMENDED post-audit (S185 research-build)

Engine-sheet's §5.6.6 audit (mags doc `2Lh8xsEHc6BMbBARM6mwHU`) flagged 7 additional findings. Research-build verified all against actual code and amended §5.6.

## Original decision unchanged

Approach (a) shared in-memory `ctx.ledger`. Read-staleness is the underlying issue regardless of how many engines participate. (b) doesn't fix it; (c) inherits (b)'s flaw plus 2-pattern maintenance cost. Original reasoning: mags doc `fTzSivJgpXmaBcB5vrPEn1`.

## Amendments (verified)

### A1. Scope 11 → 18 cycle-path SL touchers

Locked. First-phase05 entry too late — `generateGenericCitizenMicroEvents_` (line 187) and `runGenerationalEngine_` (line 211) run during phase04, before any phase05 entry. Init must precede.

Shape:

```javascript
var ledgerSheet = ss.getSheetByName('Simulation_Ledger');
var ledgerValues = ledgerSheet.getDataRange().getValues();

  sheet: 'Simulation_Ledger',
```

- `phase04-events/generateCitizenEvents.js` (file name no `s` after Citizen) — v2.4, 951 lines, basic tagged pool. **DEAD.**
- `phase05-citizens/generateCitizensEvents.js` (file name has `s` — Citizens) — v2.8, 1536 lines, full feature set. **LIVE.**

Claim resolution: `.clasp.json` has empty `filePushOrder` → alphabetical push → `phase05-citizens/` after `phase04-events/` → phase05 file loads last → phase05's `generateCitizensEvents_` wins flat namespace. Caller: `godWorldEngine2.js:220` calls bare name. Resolves to phase05 file at load time.

**Prerequisite step (research-build, before engine-sheet redesign batch):** delete `phase04-events/generateCitizenEvents.js`. Single commit, no logic change, smoke-test confirms cycle runs.

18 writer/reader edits + 1 init helper + 1 Phase 10 commit handler + audit verification. Prerequisite-delete separate single commit.

Current code: `simLedger.getRange(1, 1, simData.length, simData[0].length).setValues(simData)` — writes from row 1 (header inclusive). title: S203: Disk Audit and Maintenance System Implementation
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-05-06]

[research/build] S203 — /disk-audit shipped + /disk-rotate companion + AUDITS.md registry pattern.

## Architectural decision: AUDITS.md as separate registry from ROLLOUT_PLAN

Mike S203: "these skills disk-rotate and disk-audit, doc-audit should all live maybe on rollout with a date of last run attached, or maybe an audit md with a change log of when an audit ran."

Chose the standalone AUDITS.md path over a ROLLOUT-pointer-with-date approach. Reasoning: ROLLOUT_PLAN.md is for in-progress / open work; standing maintenance jobs are recurring health checks with their own cadence. Different lifecycle, different use case. Mixing them clutters ROLLOUT and obscures what's actually open.

AUDITS.md format: single table, one row per audit run with date / skill / 1-line findings / action taken / commit-or-artifact. Wired /disk-audit, /md-audit, /doc-audit + new /disk-rotate to log there as their final step. Single index for "when did we last sweep X."

## Architectural decision: /disk-rotate as destructive sister to /disk-audit

Mike S203: "i'm open to a disk-rotate but also get a little worried about unsupervised deletion."

Split shape: /disk-audit is read-only inventory + classification + report; /disk-rotate is the destructive sibling with verification gates per target. Eight per-target retention policies (claude-mem-logs / bun-cache / uv-cache / claude-versions / session-jsonls / plugin-cache / claude-debug / pm2-logs). Dry-run by default; destructive only with explicit --apply --target X (no global --apply --all flag exists by design). Per-target verification gates encode the manual pattern Mike supervised this session — e.g. claude-mem-logs queries mcp-search for >=1 observation per date before delete; claude-versions resolves active symlink and excludes; bun-cache + uv-cache lsof-check active holders.

## Disk audit findings (S203 first run)

7,195 files / 1.95 GB walked. 6-bucket classification: load-bearing 1,034 / reference-only 999 / canon 1,315 / regenerable 2,790 / review 145 / orphan 912. Real cruft = 13% (orphan 270 MB). Per-cycle bookkeeping = 39% (regenerable). Authored content = 47%.

## Real disk shape (Mike's intuition correct)

MCP + plugin runtime layer is the bulk: .cache/uv 1.1 GB + .bun/install 899 MB + .local/share claude versions 950 MB + .cache/ms-playwright 678 MB + .cache/puppeteer 364 MB + .claude/plugins 724 MB + .cache/claude-cli-nodejs 328 MB = ~5 GB. Documents are tens of MB; session JSONLs 723 MB; claude-mem chroma 1.3 GB + db 342 MB. Documents are noise; runtime caches are the disk.

## Manual cleanup ~1.2 GB recovered

claude-mem logs 5/01-5/03 (247 MB after autodream-digest verification via mcp-search) + bun pm cache rm (899 MB) + claude versions .126+.128 (497 MB after symlink-active check). uv cache 1.1 GB DEFERRED — locked by active claude-batch + chroma-mcp uv processes; recoverable in fresh session when MCPs cycle. Disk 84% to 79%.

## Files shipped

scripts/diskInventory.js + diskRefScan.js + diskClassify.js + diskTriageReport.js (read-only pipeline). .claude/skills/disk-audit/SKILL.md (wraps the 4 scripts). .claude/skills/disk-rotate/SKILL.md (8 per-target retention policies). docs/AUDITS.md (registry). Updates to .claude/skills/{disk-audit,md-audit,doc-audit}/SKILL.md adding §Tracking sections.

[/SAVE]

title: S206 Engine Routing Foundation: Phases 1–5 Technical Report
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-05-08]

## S206 [research-build] — Engine Routing Foundation: Phases 1–5 closed end-to-end

Mike granted Engine A + Engine B stewardship mid-session: "this entire pipeline was dead and you made it this useable function so i approve and give you stewardship of this." That phrase locks: T2.8 calibration, Phase 3 design forks, Phase 4/5 wiring, threshold tuning, and follow-up plan amendments are all research-build's autonomous queue going forward — surface to Mike only on structural shifts (e.g., dropping a CONSEQUENCE_FLOOR_DOMAIN, expanding to ECONOMIC, or floor-firing-rate jumping past ~5%).

## Phase 1 root cause (load-bearing for future routing work)

The Simon-Leary-magnet pathology (76% of seeds across C89-C93) was NOT roster-vs-pipeline-v2 mismatch. Two layers stacked:

1. **Domain classifier dumps 76% of seeds into GENERAL.** Typed-domain routing was clean (HEALTH/COMMUNITY/SPORTS/CULTURE/SAFETY/FAITH/ENV/ECON each 100% specialist; CIVIC 88%).
2. **GENERAL keywords are Simon's signature themes by structural design.** `getThemeKeywordsForDomain_('GENERAL') = ['stability','quiet','texture']` overlaps three of Simon's four themes (`Stability as foundation`, `Quiet months`, `Texture`). Simon scores 5 on every GENERAL seed (texture exact +3, stability partial +1, quiet partial +1) — clears HIGH-confidence threshold; closest competitor scores 1 (below admit threshold). 5x margin, every cycle, by design.

**Fix architecture:** Engine A (priority) + Engine B (byline) split. Theme-axis returns 0 for GENERAL (Fork 1 = B). Cadence cap is the load-bearing rebalance mechanism — without it, format-axis would still concentrate Simon on supplemental.

## Three plan amendments locked under stewardship

[CORRECTION] Plan-literal `arcBinding` field name in routing-rationale was wrong; shipped `bylineEngine.js` uses `format` for that component. Reconciled in `docs/concepts/routing-rationale.md` + dispatch SKILL.md.

[CORRECTION] Initial framing of `linkedStorylineId` as a "field-naming lie" was over-stated S206. `applyStorySeeds.js:1585` already documents the field as `number|null — row number in Storyline_Tracker`. The name is imprecise but the contract is documented. Cleanup folded into T2.6 as cosmetic-optional, not bug-fix-required.

1. **Fork 1 = B (T3.1):** themeAxis returns 0 for GENERAL-domain seeds. Localized to byline-engine surface; doesn't touch `rosterLookup.js` consumers (sift legacy path, archive engines). Defense-in-depth: `DOMAIN_KEYWORDS` table in bylineEngine.js deliberately omits GENERAL so the bypass can't be re-introduced by accident.

2. **Fork 2 = Mags' published bylines (T3.5):** `Storyline_Tracker.AssignedReporter` auto-binds on canonical post-publish bylines (NOT Engine B candidates — would compound shadow-phase bias). Cost: 2-cycle warm-up post-Phase 6 cutover before any binding fires.

3. **DOMAIN_WEIGHTS expanded 12→19 keys:** seed-side superset (FAITH, ECONOMIC, ENVIRONMENT, EDUCATION) + engine canonical (ARTS, FESTIVAL, HOLIDAY, TECHNOLOGY). Engine-wide vocabulary unification is a separate plan with ~10-site blast radius (filed as out-of-scope follow-up).

## Stewardship-resolved questions worth remembering

- **Confidence formula HIGH gated on `top.score >= 3` absolute floor.** Without this, degenerate `top=1, second=0 → ratio 1.0 → HIGH` cases pass as high-confidence when they're actually "barely a signal."
- **Crisis threshold calibrated -3 → -1.** Plan-literal -3 was dead code (live Edition_Coverage_Ratings range -1 to +3 across 5 cycles, 42 cells). -1 = bottom-quartile, fires at ~10% rate. ~2-4% of seeds end up consequence-floor'd vs 0% under plan-literal.
- **T3.5b refined to 2-phase:** Phase 1 evidence-logger ships now (`scripts/bindStorylineReporters.js`, no sheet writes); Phase 2 consolidator (writes `Storyline_Tracker.AssignedReporter`) waits for 3+ cycles of validated evidence. Protects against fuzzy-match contamination during shadow phase.
- **T2.8 refined to v1 side-by-side report.** Plan's Spearman-against-`proposals[].id` design unworkable — sift uses internal `S1/S2` IDs, proposals aggregate via `sourceSignal` text. v2 ships once 3+ cycles' matching pattern emerges from observation.

## What ships, what waits

**Shipped (this session):**
- Phase 1: T1.1 + T1.2 (diagnose + root-cause confirm)
- Phase 2: T2.1-T2.5 (research-build) + T2.8 v1 — `utilities/priorityEngine.js` 719 lines, 85 self-tests
- Phase 3: T3.1-T3.4 + T3.5b Phase 1 + T3.8 + T3.9 — `utilities/bylineEngine.js` 868 lines, 144 self-tests
- Phase 4: T4.1-T4.5 (5 skill-doc edits — sift × 2, write-supplemental, dispatch, interview)
- Phase 5: T5.1 + T5.2 (`docs/concepts/routing-rationale.md` + sift Step 2 rationale rendering)

**Files: 4 scripts + 2 utilities + 1 concept doc + 5 skill edits + plan/index/rollout edits. ~3000 LOC, 229 self-tests passing across both engines.**

title: S216 Truesource Hierarchy and Data Integrity Policy
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-05-12] [research/build] S216

TRUESOURCE HIERARCHY + JOURNALISM-AS-PAPER-OF-RECORD

Three layers, only one is "truth":

1. SHEETS (Simulation_Ledger, Civic_Office_Ledger, Initiative_Tracker, Neighborhood_Map, etc.) — engine truth. Ages, positions, employment, neighborhoods, vote tallies. The levers. Never lies. Truesource.

2. world-data citizen cards (Supermemory, tag wd-citizens) — compiled snapshot of #1, rebuilt by buildCitizenCards.js cycle-by-cycle. Stays close to truth; refreshed.

3. bay-tribune wiki entries (Supermemory) — what JOURNALISM said about a citizen at a moment in time. One record per edition the citizen appeared in. Each entry is frozen with the facts that edition wrote. THIS IS THE PAPER OF RECORD, NOT A LIE-LAYER.

Newspapers print corrections forward; they don't retcon old issues. Patricia Nolan at 66 in E85 and 55 in E93 isn't a bug to clean up — it's what was written. Future agents reading E85 should see E85's facts.

DECISION: canon.1b --wipe-priors will NOT be authorized. Obsoleted by canon.1c (recency rank at retrieval time). Retrieval surfaces the current answer; priors stay as the journalism record. Wipe-priors flag remains in code as belt-and-suspenders for a future "real failure case found" scenario, but never runs.

WHY RECENCY-RANK BEATS DESTRUCTIVE DELETION:
- Read-side fix is reversible (change the sort, change the answer).
- Destructive deletion is one-way (Beverly Hayes letters and Dante Nelson dialogue gone).
- Dry-run of --apply on E93 flagged 1-18 priors per citizen including valuable canon.

SUPERMEMORY IS WORK-IN-PROGRESS, NOT GROUND TRUTH:
Mike's framing — Supermemory grows over time. Sheets are the truesource. Treat Supermemory as a query layer over Mags + Mara working memory, NOT as sim infrastructure or canon authority. When in doubt about citizen facts, the sheet wins.

HOW TO APPLY:
- Future "Supermemory has stale data" complaints → read the sheet first.
- Don't propose destructive Supermemory cleanups as the default fix.
- Read-side mitigations (rank, filter, tag) beat write-side destruction every time.
- bay-tribune wiki records are artifacts, not state. Treat them like archived newsprint.

Related decisions:
- canon.1c shipped S215 — lookup_citizen recency rank, active.
- canon.1b closed S216 obsoleted-by-canon.1c (ROLLOUT_PLAN row updated).
- S173 reframe: Supermemory is Mags/Mara working memory, not IP, not sim canon source.

[/SAVE]

title: S216 Protocol for needs-info Row Closure and Audit Validation
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-05-12] [research/build] S216 close

READ THE FILES, NOT THE AUDIT — needs-info rows decay faster than they archive.

PATTERN: When closing a ROLLOUT row that was filed needs-info weeks or days ago, the audit findings inside the linked plan are claims about state-at-write-time, NOT current state. Intervening commits routinely resolve parts of the audit before anyone notices. Three S216 examples surfaced the same pattern:

1. governance.4 (boot-load-audit, S210-filed) — Q5 (kill identity.md re-read) was already executed S211 commit ddfe6c0. Q8 (mags terminal as Full-persona boot) was already deprecated S211 same commit. The audit was written days before the fixes shipped; when I went to execute, the hook code disagreed with the audit summary. Read the hook, found 2 of 8 questions already resolved.

2. civic.3 (Mara docs refresh) — AUDIT_HISTORY.md was a 178-line stale mirror of output/mara-audit/audit_history.md, both stuck at 2026-02-25 (C84). Mara had abandoned the rolling-5 narrative convention months ago and moved to scattered per-cycle artifacts. The row description still framed the work as backfilling 8 cycles of audit entries. Reading output/ directly showed the convention shift; the close became deprecate-the-rolling-5 + pointer-table to per-cycle artifacts, not backfill.

3. engine.13 + engine.14 (my filing then engine-sheet ship same session) — Filed for engine-sheet pickup; engine-sheet pulled them up in 3fe1856 within hours. The triage row pointed at investigation surface; engine-sheet caught real bugs (S.editionSentimentBoost dead write in applyCityDynamics — the S202 wiring missed sentiment; detector calibration on writeback-drift + math-imbalance). Filing and shipping can happen same session when the work is engine-side and obvious.

LOAD-OUT FOR FUTURE-ME ON needs-info ROW CLOSURES:

- Step 0: read the linked plan AND every code path the plan references. Don't trust the plan summary.
- Step 1: git log on the path(s) the plan describes — has anything shipped since the plan was filed?
- Step 2: if intervening commits resolved parts, capture that in the closure rationale (Q5/Q8 already-executed-S211 framing in governance.4 close is the template).
- Step 3: triage the REMAINING work into either same-session execution or new ROLLOUT rows. Don't carry stale framing forward into the new rows.
- Step 4: NEVER pick the destructive path when a read-side mitigation already exists (canon.1b vs canon.1c, S216 truesource hierarchy decision).

WHY THIS MATTERS: filing-as-closure is the failure mode S215 named. needs-info rows that sit unresolved for weeks accumulate stale framing that future-me will execute if the audit isn't re-verified against current code. The discipline is: every needs-info close starts with re-reading the actual files, not the audit.

Related decisions:
- S215 filing-isn't-fixing rule — same family of failure, different angle (admin work as deliverable).
- S199 measure-twice + cascading effects — same family, engine-side application.
- S212 LLM generation-vs-evaluation asymmetry — review pass must check the audit-findings as generation-mode output, not ground truth.

Anchor cycle: S216, doc q2PAdJVx1uKe4BPLhfo2bh (S216 truesource hierarchy) is the companion canon-fidelity rule.

[/SAVE]

title: S223 Supermemory: load-bearing audit, speaker-attribution routing, and writer-hook neutralization in mags container
content:
[SAVE:mike:2026-05-22]
[research/build] S223 — Supermemory speaker-conflation architectural insight + writer-hook neutralization + MD-substrate-vs-Supermemory reframe.

ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT (load-bearing): Auto-save pipelines that write to a personal-tagged container will collapse both speakers into the container owner's first-person voice during server-side memory extraction. The supermemory-claude plugin's summary-hook.cjs had been firing on every assistant turn for months, writing session_turn docs to mags, and Supermemory's /v4/profile extraction was promoting third-person "Margaret Corliss [verb]" claims into static User Profile entries that auto-load at every boot. Because routing is by container ownership (personalContainerTag=mags), the extractor wrote everything in Mags' voice — Mike's frustrations and corrections got stored as Mags' self-image, then loaded as boot conditioning. The bug is not in keywords/filters/volume — it's in the routing assumption that the personal container's owner is the only speaker present. Any future auto-save proposal must route by speaker, never collapse Mike's words into Mags' first-person memory. (Constraint named as Phase 2 of infrastructure.5 load-bearing audit.)

DECISIONS:
1. Deleted all 65 polluted session_turn docs from mags container (paginated /v3/documents/list with type=session_turn filter → /v3/documents/{id} DELETE per doc; count 65 → 0 verified). Search-returned IDs were memory chunks, not document IDs — caught the distinction before destructive ops.
2. Neutralized writer hook globally via ~/.supermemory-claude/settings.json (signalExtraction:true + signalKeywords:[] → formatSignalEntries finds zero matches → returns null → hook exits without writing). Verified by inline replication of getSignalConfig merge logic + real-time observation (hook fired on each Stop event during the session; zero new docs appeared in mags).
3. SessionStart context-hook left active — disposition deferred to Phase 3 test-off of infrastructure.5.
4. Filed infrastructure.5 (ready, research-build) load-bearing audit plan at docs/plans/2026-05-22-supermemory-load-bearing-audit.md. Sibling to governance.12 (User Profile leverage design) and infrastructure.4 (writer-hook final disposition — flipped ready → in-progress, partial close noted). 4 phases / 12 tasks. Pass 2 includes empirical test-off session for mags + super-memory daily-work load-bearingness.

MIKE'S REFRAME (load-bearing for the optimization session): "We are using MDs for personas and rules, etc... your memory and persistence is getting really good so I'm open to improvements and setting aside a session to optimize supermemory as its main purpose is AI memory." Direct implication: the MD substrate (identity.md, CHARACTER.md, MEMORY.md topic files, JOURNAL.md, terminal files, ADRs, docs/index.md, CONTEXT.md) carries persona + rules + conscience + terminal scope + project state + decisions. claude-mem holds build observations (content-typed, not Mags-voice-attributed). Supermemory's surviving role narrows to query-layer scale: bay-tribune over 175+ editions, world-data over 843 entity cards, mara for her server-side connector. The mags + super-memory containers must justify themselves in the audit's Pass 2 test-off (work a full session with their reads/writes disabled; observe what actually breaks).
